scenes.title: The business problem
scenes.text: Off-market property deals often stall before the first introduction. The seller wants proof the buyer can afford the deal. The buyer wants proof the seller has authority. Neither wants to reveal private documents or identity to a stranger. We start with Portuguese brokers facing repeated verification work.

scenes.title: Two passports. One private deal.
scenes.text: Deal Passport resolves that deadlock with two private passports. The buyer proves financial qualification without revealing the exact balance. The seller provides an issuer-backed authority claim. Both choose when to disclose. One shared policy controls the introduction.

scenes.title: The private deal
scenes.text: Here is the working product. This example uses synthetic credentials with genuine Stellar Testnet verification. The deal requires seven hundred and fifty thousand euros. The address, seller identity and dossier begin locked.

scenes.title: Verify the seller’s authority
scenes.text: Start with the seller. An approved reviewer attests authority to market this specific property. After confirmation, the seller requirement turns green. The address and source documents stay offchain. This is marketing authority, not proof of legal title.

scenes.title: Prove eligibility privately
scenes.text: Now the buyer chooses an issuer-backed credential and clicks Prove eligibility. The browser builds a zero-knowledge proof locally. The history shows preparation, proof generation, submission and confirmation. Stellar checks the trusted issuer, threshold, expiry and deal binding. The seller learns only that the buyer qualifies.

scenes.title: Both sides choose to disclose
scenes.text: A valid proof still does not open the dossier. The buyer consents, then the seller consents. Only when both passports and both permissions are current does the room become ready to disclose.

scenes.title: Open the protected dossier
scenes.text: Open the private dossier. Before returning it, the backend rechecks the latest contract state. The approved property details appear, while the buyer’s exact balance remains private. Withdrawing consent blocks future access.

scenes.title: The production plan
scenes.text: Finally, the production plan. React connects to Cloudflare for buyer, seller and deal verification, with D one records and private R two documents. Didit, Reclaim, Predial Online and ACTA supply identity, source evidence, property records and credentials. Local Rust and Arkworks proofs go to Stellar’s Soroban contracts. Evidence becomes credentials. Proofs establish qualification. Current consent controls disclosure. These integrations follow the MVP.
